sentences.text: You may never work a sailboat, but you’ll share the water with plenty of them, and Rule twelve is tested.
It decides between two sailing vessels, and it comes down to where the wind is.
First, when each boat has the wind on a different side, the one with the wind on her port side keeps out of the way.
Sailors call that being on port tack.
Second, when both boats have the wind on the same side, the boat to windward keeps out of the way of the boat to leeward.
Windward is the boat closer to where the wind is coming from.
If you have the wind on your port side, and you see a sailboat to windward but can’t tell which side she has the wind on, you keep out of the way.
When in doubt, the port-tack boat gives way.
And how do you know which side is windward?
For this rule, it’s the side opposite to the one where the mainsail is carried.
On a square-rigged vessel, it’s the side opposite her largest fore-and-aft sail.
So a boat with her mainsail out to starboard has the wind on her port side.
She’s on port tack, and she keeps clear.
